function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
CPU usage refers to the amount of processing power that a computer’s central processing unit (CPU) is currently consuming. It’s usually expressed as a percentage of the CPU’s total capacity. For example:

- **0 %** – The CPU is idle or doing nothing.
- **50 %** – Half of the CPU’s available cycles are being used.
- **100 %** – The CPU is fully occupied; all cores are busy.

Typical ranges:

| Usage | What it indicates |
|-------|-------------------|
| < 10 % | Idle or background tasks only |
| 10–30 % | Light usage (web browsing, document editing) |
| 30–70 % | Moderate usage (multitasking, media playback) |
| 70–90 % | Heavy usage (gaming, video rendering, large data processing) |
| > 90 % | Very heavy or saturated usage (heavy computation, malware, runaway processes) |

High CPU usage can cause a system to feel sluggish, increase heat and power consumption, and may indicate a misbehaving program or a need for more resources. Monitoring tools (Task Manager on Windows, Activity Monitor on macOS, top/htop on Linux) let you see real‑time CPU usage per process and overall.
